title: Cloud Security Concepts

header.html: 4.3 Understand cloud security: Characteristics (for example broad network access, rapid elasticity, measured service, on-demand self-service, resource pooling); Service models; Deployment models; Shared security model (for example roles and responsibilities)
the official ISC2 CC exam outline

html:
1Cloud characteristics

Cloud computing delivers computing resources as a service over the network, paid by use. The five essential characteristics are:

Characteristic Meaning
On-demand self-service The customer provisions resources alone, without a human at the provider
Broad network access Resources are reached over the network from many kinds of devices
Resource pooling The provider shares resources among many customers (multi-tenancy)
Rapid elasticity Resources scale up and down quickly to match demand
Measured service Usage is metered, so you pay for what you use
Exam tip

. Self-service, broad network access, pooling, elasticity, measured service. Pooling means many tenants on shared hardware, so isolation matters.

2Service models

Model Provider delivers Customer manages Example
Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) Virtual machines, storage, networks Operating system, applications, data A virtual server
Platform as a Service (PaaS) A platform to build and run apps Applications and data A managed database or app platform
Software as a Service (SaaS) A finished application Data, users and settings Web email, office suites

3Deployment models

Model Who uses it Note
Public cloud Many customers share the provider's infrastructure Cheapest, most elastic; less control
Private cloud One organization More control, higher cost
Hybrid cloud Public and private connected Flexibility; integration is harder
Community cloud Several organizations with shared needs (for example agencies) Shared cost and rules

4The shared responsibility model

The provider secures the cloud; the customer secures what they put in the cloud. The more the provider manages, the less the customer must do, but data and access are always the customer's.

Area IaaS PaaS SaaS
Physical data center, hardware Provider Provider Provider
Operating system and patches Customer Provider Provider
Applications Customer Customer Provider
Data, identities and access Customer Customer Customer

Always the customer: data classification, user accounts, access control and configuration. Most cloud breaches come from customer misconfiguration, such as public storage or weak access.

When hosting AI in the cloud, the same model applies: the customer protects training data, models and access.

Exam tip

. Data and identities are always the customer's responsibility, in every model. IaaS gives the most customer responsibility; SaaS the least.

Exam tip

. Public, private, hybrid, community describe who shares the cloud. IaaS, PaaS, SaaS describe what the provider delivers. Do not mix the two lists.

5Other cloud security points

Point Fact
Data location Laws may restrict where data is stored (data residency)
Service level agreement (SLA) The contract for availability and support
Vendor lock-in Hard to move away from a provider
Shadow IT Staff using cloud services without approval
Due diligence Review the provider's audits before choosing

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A customer can create a virtual server at any time from a web portal without contacting the provider. Which characteristic is this?

  • AOn-demand self-service, which needs no staff help
  • BMeasured service, which meters the usage
  • CResource pooling, which shares the hardware
  • DRapid elasticity, which scales the capacity
Show the answer

Answer: A. Provisioning resources alone, without provider staff, is on-demand self-service.

S2A web shop's capacity grows automatically during a sale and shrinks afterwards. Which characteristic is this?

  • ABroad network access, which allows any device
  • BResource pooling, which shares the resources
  • CMeasured service, which meters the usage
  • DRapid elasticity, which scales with demand
Show the answer

Answer: D. Quickly scaling resources up and down is rapid elasticity.

S3A company uses a web-based email service and manages only its users and data. Which service model is this?

  • AInfrastructure as a Service
  • BPlatform as a Service
  • CSoftware as a Service
  • DA private data center
Show the answer

Answer: C. A finished application delivered over the web, with the customer managing users and data, is SaaS.

S4In an IaaS deployment, who is responsible for patching the guest operating system?

  • AThe provider, who owns the data center
  • BThe auditor, who reviews the controls
  • CThe internet provider, who carries the traffic
  • DThe customer, who manages the operating system
Show the answer

Answer: D. In IaaS the customer manages the operating system and above, including patching.

S5Which responsibility belongs to the customer in every cloud service model?

  • ASecurity of the physical data center
  • BProtection of its own data and user access
  • CMaintenance of the provider's hardware
  • DPatching of the underlying hypervisor layer of the host
Show the answer

Answer: B. Data, identities and access always remain the customer's responsibility.

S6A company connects its own data center to a public cloud and moves workloads between them. Which deployment model is this?

  • APublic cloud only
  • BCommunity cloud
  • CPrivate cloud only
  • DHybrid cloud
Show the answer

Answer: D. A connected mix of private and public resources is a hybrid cloud.

6.2 Recall questions

R1Name the five cloud characteristics.

Show the answer

On-demand self-service, broad network access, resource pooling, rapid elasticity, measured service.

R2Who manages the operating system in PaaS?

Show the answer

The provider.

R3What is multi-tenancy?

Show the answer

Many customers sharing the same pooled resources.

R4What does the customer always secure?

Show the answer

Its data, identities and access.

R5What is a hybrid cloud?

Show the answer

Public and private clouds connected together.

R6What is shadow IT?

Show the answer

Staff using cloud services without approval.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Characteristics self-service, broad access, pooling, elasticity, measured service
Service models IaaS (OS and up is yours), PaaS (apps and data), SaaS (data and access)
Deployment public, private, hybrid, community
Shared responsibility provider secures the cloud; customer secures data, identities, configuration
